frozen_questions: What exact hieroglyphic signs occur in pBrooklyn 47.218.84 XI,11 for the expression translated by Meeks as 'un vagin en métal'?
Does the wording designate an anatomical female-genital noun, a generic vessel/container noun, or an anatomical-form object made of metal?
Does any source specify whether the metal female object receives the phallus, fits around the phallus as a sheath/case, or merely remains a separate complementary ritual object?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: Modern quotation -> Meeks line reference -> official ORAEC/AES Unicode transcription -> TLA lemma records -> sign-function control -> independent scholarly interpretation.
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: sign -> lexeme -> material -> grammar -> object ontology -> processional relation -> physical orientation -> contradiction return
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: Meeks-derived quotations count as one source family; TLA/ORAEC lexical data and independent sign-function catalogues are controls rather than duplicate votes.
method_execution.TENET_REVERSE: Test proposed physical mechanisms backward against the exact wording; no socket/sheath geometry may be inserted into the text unless a source encodes it.
method_execution.boundary: The JANUS methods organize and discriminate evidence; the authority is the ancient-text transcription, lexical corpus, sign catalogue and archaeological/iconographic evidence.

signs.description: two raised arms; kꜣ logogram/phonetic component
piece of flesh; regular classifier for a part of the body

vagina_lexeme.interpretive_pressure: Because the exact pBrooklyn token is the anatomical lexeme kꜣ.t and carries F51, a generic-vessel lexical reading is disfavored. The text names the object by female genital anatomy.

metal_lexeme.material_boundary: bjꜣ is a broad Egyptian metal/mineral term and does not by itself prove a modern metallurgical species. Do not silently narrow it to iron, bronze or copper without context/material evidence.

phrase_assessment.minimum_secure_reading: kꜣ.t m bjꜣ = a vagina/vulva expressed as being in/of metal, matching Meeks' 'un vagin en métal'.
phrase_assessment.reasoning: The noun is anatomically explicit, while the metal qualification makes literal biological tissue impossible as the immediate referent. The most economical object-level reading is a metal representation/object designated as a vagina/vulva. Whether it was shaped as an anatomical model, vessel, sheath, matrix, cult fitting or composite object requires morphology or additional wording.
phrase_assessment.important_distinction: ANATOMICAL_LEXEME != BIOLOGICAL_TISSUE; ANATOMICAL_LEXEME + METAL strongly implies an artificial cult object named for female anatomy.

primary_wording.meeks_control: The metal vagina is 'près de lui' in the Djed context and the two sisters are near the phallus.

processional_control.finding: Spieser explicitly refers to 'un vagin en métal porté en procession, en plus du phallus d’Osiris'.
processional_control.inference: The metal vagina and the phallus are at minimum distinguishable ritual objects/components. They must not be collapsed into a single fixed artifact.

cross_object_controls.detachable_phallus_figures: Independent Egyptian/Ptolemaic objects prove root-in/socket-out detachable phallus engineering in some male/Bes/Priapus figures. This cannot be transferred automatically to pBrooklyn's metal kꜣ.t.
cross_object_controls.pierced_female_figures: Intentional genital perforation exists in female fertility figurines, but no secure joined specimen currently proves that those perforations received a detachable phallus.
cross_object_controls.matrix_vessel_symbolism: Egyptian womb/matrix-to-vessel symbolism makes a receptacle function plausible, but this remains an object-function interpretation rather than the lexical meaning of kꜣ.t itself.

canonical_seal: 𓂸 THE WORD IS REALLY KꜢ.T — VAGINA/VULVA — AND THE MATERIAL IS REALLY BJꜢ — METAL. THE TEXT THEREFORE NAMES AN ARTIFICIAL METAL FEMALE-GENITAL OBJECT, NOT A GENERIC VESSEL. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THE PHALLUS IN PROCESSION; WHICH COMPONENT ENTERED OR ENCLOSED THE OTHER REMAINS UNWRITTEN. DO NOT INVENT THE JOINT. 𓂸
